paper.task: Image synthesis: an autoencoder (E, D) compresses an RGB image x into a low-dimensional latent z; a time-conditional UNet diffusion model, optionally conditioned on inputs y (text, semantic maps, images) through a domain-specific encoder τθ and cross-attention, models the latent distribution, and latent samples are decoded by D into images.

components.name: image x
components.what: input RGB image x ∈ R^{H×W×3}

provenance.quote: given an image x ∈ R H×W ×3 in RGB space

components.name: perceptual compression model (autoencoder)
components.what: autoencoder based on prior work [23]; learns a latent space perceptually equivalent to image space; regularised by KL-reg. or VQ-reg.

provenance.quote: Our perceptual compression model is based on previous work [23] and consists of an autoencoder

components.name: encoder E
components.what: encodes x into latent z = E(x); downsamples by factor f = H/h = W/w, f = 2^m

components.name: decoder D
components.what: reconstructs the image from the latent, x̃ = D(z); in the VQ-reg. variant it contains a vector quantization layer

contributions.text: explicit separation of the compressive from the generative learning phase, using an autoencoder whose latent space is perceptually equivalent to image space at lower computational cost

provenance.quote: We propose to circumvent this drawback by introducing an explicit separation of the compressive from the genera- tive learning phase

unclear: Inference sampling is only stated as 'samples from p(z) can be decoded to image space with a single pass through D'; the iterative denoising loop in latent space (starting from a normally distributed variable, T steps) is described only for generic DMs ('gradually denoising a normally distributed variable'), so the start noise z_T and the loop are not recorded as flows.
The text never states explicitly that the noise ε is added to z inside the forward process (only that z_t/x_t is 'a noisy version of the input'); noise is recorded only as the target in L_LDM.

Whether the cross-attention output is added back (residual) into the UNet feature map is not stated; only that τθ(y) is 'mapped to the intermediate layers of the UNet via a cross-attention layer'. The cross_attn -> unet_conv edge reflects that sentence, not a stated residual.

Novelty of the UNet: it is a time-conditional UNet [71] (reused architecture), but the text calls it 'the neural backbone of our model' and claims its augmentation with cross-attention; recorded as proposed. The cross-attention mechanism itself is cited [97] and recorded as reused.

The perceptual compression model is 'based on previous work [23]' (reused), yet advantage (iii) claims 'general-purpose compression models' — kept reused; the separation of phases is recorded as a training-procedure contribution with no component.

KL-reg. vs VQ-reg.: two alternative regularisation variants; VQ-reg. places a vector quantization layer within the decoder (not drawn as a separate component at overview depth). Which variant a figure should show is not decided by the text.
The losses' second inputs are not stated: the text does not say what the perceptual loss compares x̃ against or what the patch-based discriminator sees; full objective is 'in the supplement'.
Which UNet layers i carry cross-attention, how many, and the dimensions d, d_τ, M, N are not given numerically.
Equation for Attention is garbled in the extraction (softmax(QK^T/√d)·V reconstructed from the fragments 'T', '√', '· V', 'd'); superscripts (i) on W_Q, W_K, W_V were split onto separate lines.
The text's reference to 'Fig. 2' and 'Fig. 3' was not followed (blind run).
